skill.name: architecture-decision-records
skill.description: Create, review, and manage Architecture Decision Records with templates for documenting technical choices, trade-offs, status, and review workflows.
skill.summary: Create and maintain ADRs for important technical decisions.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are false positives caused by markdown fences, inline examples, and ADR templates. One bash automation section provides package-manager and adr-tools commands that could install software or write repository files if followed. The hardcoded URLs are reference links, and no prompt-injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: State that package installation and adr-tools commands require explicit user approval before execution. Keep the manual ADR workflow usable without running shell commands.
Keep external links as optional references only. Do not require network access for creating, reviewing, or maintaining ADRs.

content.value_statement: Technical decisions lose context when trade-offs stay in chats or tickets. This skill guides teams through ADR templates, review checklists, and lifecycle management.
actual_capabilities: Provides standard, lightweight, Y-statement, deprecation, and RFC-style ADR templates.
Guides context, decision drivers, options, rationale, consequences, and references.
Shows ADR status flow, directory structure, and README index patterns.
Includes a review checklist for submission, review, and post-acceptance steps.
Provides adr-tools command examples for ADR setup, creation, superseding, table of contents, and linking.
limitations: Does not validate whether a proposed architecture is technically correct.
Does not choose ADR numbers or file paths without project context.
Command examples require installed adr-tools and explicit approval before running.
External reference links may change outside the skill author control.

use_cases.title: Record a Technology Choice
use_cases.description: Draft an ADR that captures options, drivers, rationale, and consequences for a major platform decision.

use_cases.title: Standardize Decision Reviews
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable review process for architectural decisions before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Onboard Engineers to Past Decisions
use_cases.description: Use ADR indexes and linked records to explain why existing systems use specific technologies.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic ADR
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for documenting one clear decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ADR for this decision: [decision]. Include status, context, options, decision, rationale, and consequences.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Architecture Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for evaluating trade-offs before choosing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me compare these options for an ADR: [options]. Identify decision drivers, pros, cons, risks, and an evidence-based recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Supersede an Existing ADR
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for replacing a previous decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an ADR that supersedes [existing ADR]. Explain what changed, the new decision, migration impact, risks, and links to related ADRs.

prompt_templates.title: Design an ADR Governance Process
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for team-wide documentation standards.
prompt_templates.prompt: Define an ADR process for [team or project]. Include when to write ADRs, review roles, status rules, file naming, and index maintenance.

output_examples.input: We need to choose a primary database for an e-commerce platform.
output_examples.output: A complete ADR draft with context, decision drivers, considered options, the selected database, rationale, risks, and references.

output_examples.input: We are replacing MongoDB user profiles with PostgreSQL.
output_examples.output: A deprecation ADR that names the superseded decision, explains the migration plan, lists consequences, and records lessons learned.

output_examples.input: Review our ADR draft before we open a pull request.
output: Gaps in context and decision drivers are identified.
Missing alternatives and weak trade-off analysis are called out.
Review checklist items are organized for the pull request.

best_practices: Include rejected options and real trade-offs.
Supersede accepted ADRs with new records instead of rewriting history.
anti_patterns: Using ADRs for minor implementation details.
Hiding negative consequences or rejected alternatives.
Running optional automation commands without review and approval.

faq.question: What is an Architecture Decision Record?
faq.answer: An ADR is a short document that records the context, decision, and consequences of an important technical choice.

faq.question: When should I create an ADR?
faq.answer: Create one for significant technology choices, architecture patterns, security decisions, or decisions that future teams must understand.

faq.question: Does this skill run tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It includes command examples, but any command execution should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which ADR formats does it support?
faq.answer: It includes standard MADR, lightweight ADR, Y-statement, deprecation, and RFC-style formats.

faq.question: Can it decide the architecture for me?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure analysis and documentation, but humans must validate evidence and approve decisions.

faq.question: How should accepted ADRs be updated?
faq.answer: Do not rewrite accepted ADRs. Create a new ADR that supersedes or deprecates the old record.
